name: Fat Man's Misery
beta: Start up a neighbouring route to a terrace and set a belay, then shuffle thirty feet through the cave behind it to reach the far-side anchors and rappel. A very large cam is handy for the belay.
overview: An unusual easy outing that starts up a neighbouring route, then crawls through a cave to reach anchors on the far side of the formation.

current.area_walk_in: The way in passes through a rock arch. Ten feet beyond it, on the left, a wall carries several bolt lines.

name: Father and Son
beta: Ascend the flake, leaning on face edges to the left. A few jams near the finish gain a terrace holding the bolted anchors.
overview: A well-liked starter trad route that follows a left-facing dihedral, with solid gear, mostly juggy holds on the face and just a couple of jams.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: First Time
beta: Start from a boulder and pull through the surprisingly good holds on dark stone, finishing at the anchors.
overview: An enjoyable line on black stone beside an inside corner, with surprisingly good holds.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: 25 ft beyond the line before, up dark stone beside a corner; start from atop a boulder

name: Flour Power
beta: Pull through a roof into steep climbing, reaching a more upright section with an excellent shaking-out spot on a tiny shelf. The overhanging headwall comes next; aim for a faint corner high up, recover below it as best you are able, then lunge rightward and finish at the chains.
overview: A roof gives onto a steep wall that gradually lies back, with a decent recovery spot on a little shelf. Above that the headwall overhangs again and heads for a subtle groove; recover as best you can beneath it, then cut across to the right and finish.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Breaks through a roof sitting 8 ft over from BOHICA

name: Flux Capacitor
beta: Begin on a flake, gain a shelf, then work the upright ribs until you reach a reasonable stance. One bulge remains before the anchors.
overview: A line people tend to feel strongly about, either way. It begins up a flake onto a ledge, then works a ribbed vertical section to a reasonable stance and goes over a bulge to the finish.

current.area_walk_in: Walk toward the right from Madness Cave to reach a lower, less steep wall holding many lines. The first line met is The Sauce, beside a large tree that grows against the cliff.

name: Forearm Follies
beta: Climb the heavily featured face on bolts as far as a ledge-like break where ferns grow, about eighty feet up. Lowering from there makes a nice shorter route.
overview: A long, heavily featured line. The lower version follows bolts up the face to a level break holding a patch of ferns and the first anchors; it is graded 5.11 and highly rated.

current.area_walk_in: Cross the wooden footbridge and keep straight; a branch heads right about 20 feet beyond it. Follow that path uphill roughly ten minutes to the wall.

name: Forearm Follies (2nd anchor)
beta: Go beyond the lower anchors, over the crux bulge and into steeper stone, finishing at the upper pair of anchors. Plan on a 60 m rope to lower from the top.
overview: Beyond the fern-filled break, the crux bulge and steeper stone lead to a second anchor set; this is the harder 5.12 version of the line.

name: Fuzzy Undercling
beta: Solve the bouldery opening, then cruise upward on enormous holds to the chains.
overview: A bouldery start, then enormous holds carry you up to chained anchors.

name: G2 the Friction
beta: Leap into the offwidth and stay in it until it ends, then drift rightward to a pine and back leftward into the flared crack for the finish. Expect long gaps between protection.
overview: An offwidth facing right that starts at ground level, followed by a wander across the upper wall past a pine and into a flared crack. Gear is sparse in places.

current.area_walk_in: Go straight back from the clearing about 100 feet until an old logging track branches up the hillside leftward. Follow it 150 feet, then turn up the slope to the right along a barely visible path angling right up to a ridge. Turn right on top and follow the ridge trail for roughly five minutes until a small pinnacle shows at the cliff's end. Go left around the pinnacle to the main wall for the left-side routes, or loop around toward the wall's right-hand portion for the others.

name: Ghost in the Machine
beta: Work up sloping holds onto a spacious shelf, then step off it into a short steeper stretch that ends at the chains.
overview: An enjoyable line, the first one on the largest east-looking face. Sloping holds lead to a big ledge, then a brief steeper section.

name: God Save the Queen
beta: Use the crack for a move or two, then step left onto the slim arete and its generous holds. Place your gear while still in the crack, then climb on to the spacious ledge.
overview: A short trad line that begins in a crack, then swaps onto a slim arete with jug-sized holds and ends on a large ledge.

name: Golden Road
beta: A tough opening gives way to entertaining sequences, then a blank stretch higher up. A giant hueco offers a stance with a fine view at the anchors.

name: Government Cheese
beta: Step off a boulder to get started, then slap and pull your way upward using side-pulls and undercuts on the bolted wall until the chains.
overview: A short bolted face worked mostly on side-pulls and undercuts, entered from a handy boulder.

overview: A slab line that works as a short outing to the lower anchors, or can be stretched with four extra bolts to an upper pair of anchors.

name: High Noon

overview: Ease along the arete, then step off rightward onto the wall close to the end for a finish that makes your legs shake.

name: Hot For Teacher
beta: Shuffle rightward along a slim shelf for the first clip, then follow pockets across a blank-looking stretch toward a huge cave. Hand-traverse a little rightward along the cave's lower lip, then crank over the arched roof to the chains.
overview: After the ledge crossing, pockets lead over a seemingly holdless section into the underside of a giant cave. A hand-traverse along the cave floor line sets up a pull through the curving roof and a finish at the chains.

overview: Takes off from the same place as Rock Wars, then tracks a flake curving left across to Autumn's anchor.

name: Inhibitor
beta: The thin crack, sized for hands, pumps you out until the chimney looms and the sequence becomes unclear; plug a large cam and fight into the squeeze. Slot a bigger cam overhead when you can, then creep out to a good jam where it narrows. Fists and forearms take you to a final good jam, and from there pace yourself upward.
overview: Huge left-facing dihedral with a Yosemite flavor. A thin hand-sized crack leads to an overhanging chimney, then a constriction with a good jam, then wider fist-sized and forearm-burning cracks to the finish. Sustained and tiring.

current.area_walk_in: The walk to the wall is short, about five minutes.
current.descent: lower from bolted anchors

name: Injured Reserve
beta: Large holds precede a crux on sloping holds; beyond it, kinder holds carry you to the anchors.
overview: Large holds lead up to a crux on sloping holds, after which friendlier holds continue to the finish. The upper wall is grey and pocketed.

name: Insanity Ceiling
beta: Descend a bit from the belay tree and traverse right, then rise to a platform under a thin crack cutting the roof. Stretch beyond the lip for reasonable holds, then let your feet swing free and crank over. Slap through long stretches to sloping pockets and twin thin cracks, layback along thin edges into a hand crack, then fire for the summit.
overview: An exposed climb that crosses a roof as long as a climber's body, sitting above the lower pitch of a neighbouring route. Beyond it come thin layback edges, then jams and the summit.

name: Lucifer
beta: The first moves are relatively easy up to bolt three. A bouldery leftward kick reaches a quick shake, then a harder bouldery section leads to a decent rest. The final redpoint run goes to the break, and a short finish follows.

A harder boulder sequence brings a so-so rest at bolt five, followed by a long redpoint effort to the break and the finish.
